body:
The size tripwire now honors a declared over-run instead of flagging every file past 800 lines, and several swallowed-enumeration holes in the gate tooling now fail loud instead of silently passing.

### Added
- The size tripwire (`hooks/rot-canary-touch.js`) no longer flags a source file crossing `tripwireMaxLines` if it carries a top-of-file declaration (`// ponytail: <N> lines at declaration — <why>`, or the existing `waiver:` idiom) — implementing the amended rule that 800 lines is a review signal, not a cap; the finding is an UNDECLARED over-run only. The declaration match is bounded against a measured ReDoS: an unbounded pattern took 5.4s on a poison line reachable at shipped defaults, bounded to ~59ms.

### Fixed
- [Developer tooling only — nothing shipped changes.] Three swallowed-enumeration holes closed in the gate scripts: `manifest.mjs`'s install-manifest walk could silently omit a file from its integrity hash, letting later tamper on that file report falsely clean; `consistency.mjs`'s doctrine-mirror check now fails loud (rather than silently passing) when a rule tree can't be read or enumerated at all, not only when it's absent; and that same check now compares every file in the rule tree instead of a hard-coded 2-file pair list, so a rule outside that pair could previously diverge unnoticed between what Claude and other agents read.

### Changed
- Test files are out of scope for the size tripwire (basename and directory-segment conventions, source files only — a test file's cohesion unit is the module under test, not a line count). The PowerShell fallback twins keep the plain line count (named divergence).

body:
The memory-drift exit-gate advisory (added in v3.12.0) is no longer a loud rot-canary finding — it moves to a quiet, non-blocking channel.

### Changed
- The advisory no longer rides the blocking Stop `reason` that triggers the scan report and fix menu; it now emits on the quiet, model-only `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext` channel instead — no severity table, no fix-menu offer, no block of its own. The loud code-scan report is unchanged. The two are decoupled: the scan report keys off files still present at stop time, the drift check keys off whether MEMORY.md was ever touched this session — so a session that edited code, deleted it, and never updated MEMORY.md now surfaces only the quiet note. Detection and guards (the `memoryDriftNudge` off-switch, the root-`MEMORY.md` probe, the `.memmoved` satisfier) are unchanged. On Antigravity the Stop hook still emits the no-op `{}` — no Stop-inject channel there, so the drift note is silent on AG.

body:
rot-canary no longer records or scans files living under `os.tmpdir()`.

### Fixed
- The touch hook records nothing when an edited file resolves to inside `os.tmpdir()` — dogfood-found: a long session's throwaway one-shot harness files live in the scratchpad, which sits inside the OS temp dir, and every stop-scan was nagging on them. The check runs before both the MEMORY.md marker branch and the watched-extension gate, is boundary-safe (a sibling directory that merely prefix-matches the temp path is not wrongly excluded), and is a scan-scope refinement rather than a security boundary.

body:
Hardens the v3.12.0 memory-drift marker write against a TOCTOU race and a symlink-write hazard (CodeQL `js/insecure-temporary-file`, alerts #55/#56).

### Security
- The `.memmoved` marker write is now a single atomic `wx` (create-only) file open, replacing an `existsSync` pre-check plus a plain write — the old sequence had a TOCTOU window and could write through a pre-planted symlink at the marker path. A pre-existing marker (already recorded this session) is now an expected `EEXIST`, swallowed the same as before; a symlink at the path is refused. Behavior is otherwise unchanged.

body:
The rot-canary Stop hook gains a memory-drift exit-gate advisory: a session that edited code but never touched MEMORY.md gets a one-line nudge before it ends.

### Added
- The touch hook records a MEMORY.md edit (any directory, basename match) as a marker, checked before the watched-code-extension gate so a non-code MEMORY.md edit still counts. At session end, if code moved this session and no such marker exists, the Stop hook appends one localized advisory line (all 5 languages) to the existing scan nudge. It fires only when the project already uses the MEMORY.md convention (a read-only existence probe), rides the existing scan nudge rather than firing standalone, and never blocks on its own — the Antigravity Stop hook still emits its existing no-op. Named v1 limitations, not fixed here: a version-bump-only session (no watched code file touched) emits nothing; the check is session-global, not per-repo; it is silenced by rot-canary's own `manual`/`off` modes.
- `memoryDriftNudge` config key (boolean, default `true`) — the standing off-switch for the advisory above.

### Fixed
- `cadence.md` and `escalation.md` freshness stamps refreshed to reflect a re-read against current hook behavior; no content drift found beyond the stamp date.

body:
The Antigravity adapter now emits the current Antigravity hook-inject contract; the old pilot-era shape never actually delivered anything.

### Fixed
- The conductor's PreInvocation output on Antigravity is now `{"injectSteps":[{"ephemeralMessage":...}]}`, re-derived against the current AG build's hooks documentation — the pilot-era `additionalContext` key was a dead letter on the current engine (zero hits; it never delivered). The Stop hook now emits an explicit no-op `{}` on AG, since the current engine documents no Stop-output inject channel; its other side effects (the ack marker, the stale-marker sweep) still run, and AG users reach findings via the manual `/rot-canary` path. CoalMine still never blocks on AG.
- All three hooks now read the session key `conversationId` first (with the legacy `session_id`/`sessionId`/transcript-path fallbacks kept), and the conductor and touch hook resolve the workspace from `workspacePaths[0]`. Tier unchanged: wired, not yet live-validated in a real AG session.

body:
The installer no longer deletes a directory it does not own before writing to it.

### Fixed
- [HIGH] A no-manifest install used to fall back to hard-coded skill names and delete each one outright — if a name collided with a foreign, unrelated directory, the install destroyed that user's data. The installer now proves ownership before removing anything (the directory is absent, empty, listed in the package manifest, or carries CoalMine's own marker file) and refuses a foreign collision fail-loud instead of deleting it; an owned install still upgrades normally. Found by a CoalBoard audit — the underlying defect spanned three separate delete sites in the installer, not only the one the audit originally named.

body:
The conductor's onboarding offer now self-silences on a repo that has already run gold-standard, and the plugin gains a description-length gate shared across the flock.

### Changed
- The conductor's onboarding line auto-suppresses once any verified gold-standard stamp exists anywhere in the repo's rule roots (a `skipOnboarding` config key still forces it off explicitly) — decided against the same working directory each platform's own freshness scan already uses, so the suppression can't silently check the wrong repo on a platform whose hook process starts outside the workspace.
- `verify.mjs` gains a shared description-length gate: every skill and command's frontmatter `description` (+ `when_to_use`) must stay at or under 1024 characters, the cross-platform-safe cap used flock-wide.

body:
Closes a symlink residual left open by v3.11.0's TOCTOU fix on the Antigravity marker write (CodeQL `js/insecure-temporary-file`).

### Security
- `mkdirSync`'s recursive mode silently follows a symlink pre-planted at the marker subdirectory — the directory's `0o700` permission mode is never applied to a pre-existing path, so the earlier atomic-create fix could still write through an attacker-planted symlink into a location outside CoalMine's control. An explicit no-follow check now refuses a symlink at that subdirectory and fails closed (skips the emit) instead. This completes the mitigation v3.11.0 began.

body:
Five more platforms gain hook-configs, Gemini CLI reaches full session-start auto-cadence, file-copy installs get an honest conductor mode, and four CodeQL HIGHs are closed at source.

### Added
- Five new platform hook-configs: GitHub Copilot CLI, Kiro, Augment, Devin CLI (Devin-CLI-only, not Devin Desktop/Cascade), and JetBrains Junie (SessionStart-only — no per-tool events exist there). All five carry the works-with tier; any unverified response channel is marked as such.
- A new `FileCopy` conductor mode for the five platforms above: rule-freshness nudges only — the plugin-update offer and the shared update-check stamp are excluded, both being Claude-Code-plugin machinery, so a file-copy install never consumes the update stamp a co-installed Claude Code depends on.
- `kiro` and `augment` install targets.
- Gemini CLI now reaches full auto-cadence through its genuine `SessionStart` event, emitting Gemini's own nested inject shape (its only SessionStart channel — the flat shape used elsewhere would be silently dropped there). Wired, not yet live-validated.

### Fixed
- Gemini CLI's docs reconciled across five spots — retires a stale "superseded by Antigravity CLI" framing; Gemini CLI remains a business-tier product with its own 11-event hook surface, and only the individual-tier product line ended.
- The Antigravity once-per-session marker write is now an atomic create in a private permission-restricted temp subdirectory, replacing a check-then-write sequence that had a TOCTOU race.
- The stale-marker sweep gained a second pass for the new marker location and now runs before rot-canary's own mode gates — conductor markers are collected on every stop even when rot-canary itself is off or manual; the canary's own temp files stay mode-gated.

### Security
- Closes four CodeQL HIGH alerts (`js/insecure-temporary-file` ×2, `js/file-system-race` ×2) at source.

### Notes
- Supersedes v3.7.9's "the sweep runs only on the active path" note: that was true when written, but the Antigravity port later added conductor markers, a separate class the sweep now also collects on every stop even when rot-canary is off or manual — the canary's own temp files are still mode-gated exactly as v3.7.9 described.

Gate: build + verify + `hooks.test.mjs` 38/38 + `conductor-update.test.mjs`/`consistency.test.mjs` 30/30 PASS.
